bull_bear.body:
- Maintained the no. 1 position in ignition systems for the past three years while consistently expanding its customer base across ICE and EV segments.
- Long-standing OEM partnerships built over four decades of supply - major customers are TVS Motor Company Limited, Hero MotoCorp Limited and Bajaj Auto Limited, with a supply history spanning TVS-Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, Hero Motors, Royal Enfield, Piaggio, Honda Motorcycle and others.
- Innovation-led manufacturing base of three strategically located state-of-the-art facilities plus an advanced Technical Center and a dedicated R&D center.
- Debt-free balance sheet maintained despite higher working capital needs, with working capital days reduced from 42 to 40, providing flexibility to invest in technology, automation, manufacturing expansion and new product development.
- Supply-chain resilience from proactive planning, localized/diversified sourcing and lower dependence on imported rare-earth magnet content in key products, which limited disruption during geopolitical volatility.
- Broadening electronics portfolio (ISG systems, sensors, ECUs, DC-DC, static converters) aligned with rising electronic content per vehicle, evidenced by business nominations secured from major OEMs for EFI ECU, ISG systems, GPS sensors and crank position sensors.
- Export and global reach - products sold in over 10 countries, exports at 8% of turnover, a growing North America customer base, and traction for ignition systems and sensors in stationary engine applications.
- Technology access through patents registered for EV applications, a global technical tie-up for ECG and EFU, and a partnership with Athena, Italy for EFI.
- Aftermarket distribution strength - stronger dealer engagement, expanded distribution reach, localized stocking strategies and improved product availability across domestic and export aftermarket channels.
- Strong promoter/group backing - Lucas Indian Service Limited holds 70.32% (raised via acquisition of MEDJ and MHIPL's 44.15 Lakh shares, 19.51%), with SB TVS Industrial Ventures Private Limited as ultimate holding company.
- Value-based differentiation rather than pure cost competition, supported by an improved sales mix with higher contribution from exports and aftermarket sales.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration and low export footprint — MD&A Customer Risk: high dependence on a limited number of key customers can create vulnerabilities if these relationships change; in addition, limited awareness and proactive pursuit of emerging business opportunities could constrain growth prospects, and a relatively low export footprint elevates exposure to geopolitical risks, potentially affecting operations and profitability. BRSR names the major customers as TVS Motor Company Limited, Hero MotoCorp Limited and Bajaj Auto Limited, and puts the contribution of exports at 8% of total turnover. Mitigation is expanding market reach through direct sales and strategic partnerships alongside exploration of export opportunities, with dependency on key customers progressively reduced over the years.
- Supplier concentration - single-source vendors and undiversified import base — MD&A Supplier Risk: heavy reliance on single-source vendors and limited geographic diversification among import suppliers creates supply chain risk; while lead times for electronic components have improved, automotive parts continue to face longer lead times. Mitigation is strategic sourcing initiatives for high-risk vendors and expanding indexation coverage for commodities not currently included in customer settlements.
- Input cost volatility - silver and electronic components — MD&A Input Cost Volatility Risk: fluctuating prices of silver and electronic components can increase production costs and pressure profit margins; mitigation is long-term supplier agreements, VAVE, strategic inventory management and continuous cost monitoring. The Board's Report adds that a sharp increase in commodity prices during the fourth quarter exerted pressure on margins, that freight cost escalations and continued depreciation of the Indian Rupee may exert pressure on margins in the near term, and that the Company is pursuing compensation from customers through price revisions and indexing arrangements for currently non-indexed commodities.
- Technology obsolescence and the EV transition — MD&A Technology Risk: rapid technological change necessitates continuous innovation and adaptability; heightened EV competition from both established players as well as startups underscores the importance of differentiation; and there is a significant risk of product obsolescence as evolving technologies require ongoing upgrades to sustain market relevance. The industry section adds that electrification, connected mobility and software-defined vehicles demand significant and sustained capital investment, and that players lacking scale, localization capabilities or financial resilience may struggle to remain competitive. Mitigation: strategic technology partnerships in specialized areas, leveraging OEM relationships, and ongoing R&D investment.
- Geopolitical disruption - rare earth supply chain and Red Sea logistics — MD&A Geopolitical Risk: tensions between the US and China have heightened rare earth supply chain risks, and maritime disruptions in the Red Sea driven by West Asia conflicts have intensified logistical delays and increased input costs, creating a highly challenging operating environment; the mitigation note also cites anticipated impacts arising from labor code reforms. Mitigation is execution excellence, disciplined cost optimization including Value Analysis and Value Engineering (VAVE), and increased adoption of ferrite magnets as an alternative to rare earth materials. The Board's Report confirms West Asia developments contributed to inflationary pressures and supply chain constraints in the availability of certain raw materials, and BRSR lists Global Geo-political as a material risk-and-opportunity issue with a plan in place to de-risk the supply chain.
- Semiconductor and critical mineral dependency concentrated in limited geographies — MD&A industry section: increasing reliance on semiconductors and battery-grade critical minerals, concentrated within limited global geographies, exposes the industry to supply-side vulnerabilities; while Indian OEMs demonstrated relative resilience during the pandemic, the shift toward electrified and software-driven architectures materially amplifies this risk.
- IT and cyber risk - protective measures stated to be currently inadequate — MD&A IT and Cyber Risk states existing measures to protect confidential and sensitive information from internal and external threats are currently inadequate, and BRSR lists Data Security and Privacy as a material risk citing an inadequate information security and cyber framework. Mitigation: a completed Security Incident and Event Management audit with corrective measures implemented, a successfully completed Information Security Management System surveillance audit, regular cybersecurity awareness programmes, and audit trails established across all critical business applications. No security breaches or system outages were reported during the year.
- People risk - talent attraction, retention and organisational alignment — MD&A People Risk: challenges in attracting and retaining top talent may impact long-term growth, and a misalignment between the organizational structure and strategic objectives could affect operational efficiency. BRSR discloses a permanent employee turnover rate of 15.68% in 2025-26 versus 15.19% in 2024-25 (permanent workers nil). Mitigation is strengthening employer branding, enhancing training and development programs to build leadership capabilities, and a focused approach on defining key result areas.

business.body: INEL manufactures electronic ignition systems and advanced mechatronic products - ignition coils, AC generators/flywheel magnetos, integral units, regulators and rectifiers, controllers/ECUs including Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) systems, sensors and static converters - for OEMs in the automotive and non-automotive domains. It describes itself as a manufacturer within the automotive industry, with manufacturing accounting for 91% of turnover, and caters to two-wheeler, three-wheeler, general purpose engine, all-terrain vehicle, snow mobile and recreational vehicle applications, its major customers being TVS Motor Company Limited, Hero MotoCorp Limited and Bajaj Auto Limited. Production runs from three strategically located manufacturing facilities supported by an advanced Technical Center, and the Company is also building an aftermarket and export business, with exports contributing 8% of total turnover.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Electronic Ignition Systems:** Electronic Ignition Magnetos, Ignition Coil, Integral Unit (IU), AC Generator / Flywheel Magneto (ACG), Regulator and Rectifier, Digital CDI ignition system, CDI-cum-flasher unit for 4S motorcycle, Multi-pole flywheel magnetos and regulator
- **Controllers:** Electronic Control Units (ECUs) and modules, Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) System, EFI ECU, ICE+ products (high efficiency, ISG Systems)
- **Sensors:** Sensors, GPS sensors using ferrite magnet technology, Crank position sensors
- **EV and advanced electronics:** DC-DC (entry in EV segment), Static Converters, Display
- **Other:** Automobile lighting spares, Electronic Ignition Magnetos - Others

outlook.body:
- Transform INEL into a future-focused mobility electronics company by strengthening market leadership and expanding technology capabilities.
- Run a balanced powertrain strategy - strengthen core ICE technologies while investing in EV and advanced electronics capabilities - to participate across the full spectrum of evolving mobility ecosystems.
- Expand the electronic product portfolio (ignition systems, Integrated Starter Generator products, sensors) and deepen penetration into premium vehicle segments.
- Strategically enhance participation in the premium and high-value two-wheeler category through differentiated, high-performance solutions that improve efficiency, reliability and overall vehicle performance.
- Grow the export business by expanding the customer base and application footprint across North America and other overseas markets, including ignition systems and sensors for stationary engine applications.
- Keep innovation and engineering excellence central to long-term growth; the Company registered patents for EV applications during the year and continues to evolve its technology roadmap in line with future mobility requirements.
- Explore global technical partnerships to accelerate time-to-market and enhance access to emerging technologies while preserving operational excellence.
- De-risk sourcing through strategic and localized sourcing, alternate engineering solutions, disciplined inventory planning, supplier alignment, a strong domestic supplier ecosystem and lower dependence on imported rare-earth magnet content in key products.
- Improve cost competitiveness through automation, low-cost manufacturing solutions, process optimization and productivity improvement programs.
- Advance digitization through improved systems integration, ERP implementation, commodity tracking tools and enhanced data-driven decision-making frameworks.
- Scale the aftermarket business through stronger dealer engagement, expanded distribution reach, localized stocking strategies, improved product availability and portfolio expansion across both domestic and export aftermarket channels.
- Compete on value-based differentiation rather than pure cost competition.
- Continue investing ahead of demand through capacity enhancement, smart manufacturing initiatives and operational digitization programs, funded by a debt-free balance sheet and financial discipline.
- Recover commodity cost inflation by pursuing compensation mechanisms with customers through price revisions and by extending indexing arrangements to commodities that are currently non-indexed.
- Distribution is handled as a single interim dividend that is then confirmed as the final dividend rather than a separate final payout: the Board declared an interim dividend at its meeting on 13th February 2026 and the directors recommend consideration of the same as the final dividend for the year, with the Notice of the 41st AGM putting it to members only to be noted and confirmed as the final dividend for the year ended 31st March 2026. On group structure, the Company states it does not have any Joint venture or Associate Company, and its only subsidiary (PT Automotive Systems Indonesia) completed winding up with liquidation proceeds received in June 2025 - so capital sits in the standalone Indian business rather than in overseas arms; the audited financial statements of the subsidiary are placed on the Company's website and made available to members on request. Managing Director remuneration, including its commission element, is approved by the Board on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and within the limits approved by shareholders at the AGM. On philosophy, the Company says it 'remains committed to enhancing long-term shareholder value through transparent and responsible business practices, without compromising on integrity, regulatory compliance, or social commitments', with Corporate Governance encompassing responsible oversight of business strategies and financial discipline. The routed extract contains no explicit payout-ratio, buyback, debt-reduction, credit-rating or reinvestment policy statement.
- Occupational Health and Safety Management is identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: ISO 45001 implemented for the Health and Safety Management System with EOHS certification, a Weekly Safety Audit carried out zone-wise by the Safety Team with work-related hazards identified, a Safety Committee meeting every alternate month, and an external agency engaged once a year for an overall safety study; stated financial implication is zero fatality or loss of asset and adherence to legal compliance.
- Climate change impact on products is identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk - climate change affects availability of raw materials, power and natural resources like water; the Company has an internal risk framework for raw-material risks, continues to invest in renewable energy, and has an internal environment framework that monitors Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.
- All three manufacturing facilities - Hosur (Tamil Nadu), Puducherry and Rewari (Haryana) - are certified under ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 standards.
- Data Security and Privacy: a SIEM (Security Incident Event Management) study was conducted with counter-measures implemented, an ISMS 27001 surveillance audit was conducted to ensure no non-conformances, cybersecurity awareness programmes are run through various forums, and audit trails have been established across all critical business applications; no security breaches or system outages were reported during the year.
- CSR: the Board approved ` 130.25 Lakhs, i.e., 2% of the average qualifying net profits of the last three financial years; after setting off the previous year's excess spent of ` 8.98 Lakhs the balance ` 121.26 Lakhs was required to be spent, against which the Company spent ` 129.48 Lakhs - ` 8.21 Lakhs in excess of the CSR obligation, to be carried forward to FY 2026-27. Most non-Section-135 sustainability/responsible-business activities were carried out near the factory locations.
- Gender diversity: 2 of 6 Board of Directors are female (33.333%) and 1 of 3 Key Management Personnel is female (33.333%); the workforce is 441 women out of 2,601 (17%), split 11% women among supervisors and managers, 20% among union employees, 17% among associates and 23% among contract.
- Human capital investment: 15,539 employee hours spent in training, 1,244 employees attended training and 68 training types were offered, with focus areas including Application of AI in Manufacturing, mechatronics and integrated automotive technologies, and lean manufacturing and zero-defect quality practices through ACMA-led initiatives; high-potential employees are groomed through the Lucas TVS Leadership Institute, and effective from 2026-27 INEL values and leadership behaviors will be integrated into the performance assessment framework with defined weightage.
- Employee Training & Development and Employee Well-Being are identified in the BRSR material-issues table as opportunities - high-potential employees have been identified and an external consultant partnered to deliver specialized training to nurture future leaders; a compensation benchmarking exercise in 2025-26 was followed by market correction and performance-linked compensation revisions that enhanced retention particularly within Research & Development, and the Employee Referral Scheme contributed 31% of total hires during the year.
- Governance is identified in the BRSR material-issues table as both a risk and an opportunity - the dynamic compliance landscape is a risk if compliance is not monitored and adhered to on time; the Company uses a Compliance tool to monitor the regulatory and compliance landscape, with positive stated implications.
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone; the name of the assurance provider and the type of assurance obtained are both stated as 'Not applicable' (no external BRSR assurance). Policies cover each of the nine NGRBC principles, but Board approval is recorded as 'No' for P2, P6, P7 and P9.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for all stakeholder groups; complaints filed in 2025-26 were 1 from Shareholders and 1 from Employees and Workers (2 in 2024-25), with nil from Communities, Investors, Customers and Value Chain Partners, and none pending resolution at the close of the year.
- Diversity, inclusion and workplace conduct: a zero-tolerance approach towards harassment and discrimination with an escalation mechanism administered through an external agency to ensure impartiality; the safety framework is supported by Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), Occupational Control Procedures and Fire Risk Assessments conducted at regular intervals.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: India Nippon Electricals (INEL) describes an already-built manufacturing footprint rather than a named greenfield project pipeline. The Company operates manufacturing facilities plus an advanced Technical Center, with its original manufacturing unit established at Hosur, Tamil Nadu; the report records ISO TS16949:2002 certification for 'all three manufacturing locations of INEL', and the Hosur facility received gold certification under the CII GreenCo rating system. In the most recent phase of its journey timeline the Company records the 'Introduction of ISG machine, opening of a new R&D center, and expansion of manufacturing plant', and states it has 'Completed factory expansion with ongoing capacity enhancements' - i.e. the physical expansion is done and what continues is incremental capacity enhancement, with no commissioning date, cost or capacity number attached. Product-line expansion is the other axis: 'Expansion into new product lines: sensors, display, entry in EV segment through DC-DC', introduction of new products including sensors and ICE+ products (high efficiency, ISG Systems), a global technical tie-up for ECG and EFU, and a partnership with Athena, Italy for EFI. During the year the Company incurred market development expenses for future product lines including sensors, registered patents for EV applications, and says it is 'exploring global technical partnerships to accelerate time-to-market and enhance access to emerging technologies'. Geographic expansion runs through exports rather than overseas plants: INEL's products reach customers in over 10 countries, with deeper penetration across North America, Europe and ASEAN, acquisition of new customers in North America, and sharpened aftermarket capabilities; the Company states an 'Increased strategic focus on exports and the aftermarket segment to drive growth'. Capability build-out during the year was in automation, low-cost manufacturing solutions, process optimization and productivity improvement, plus digitization through improved systems integration, ERP implementation and commodity tracking tools. On the structural side the footprint contracted rather than grew overseas: the subsidiary PT Automotive Systems Indonesia (PTASI) completed its winding-up process and the liquidation proceeds were received on 24th June 2025. Renewable energy (wind energy usage) is noted in the journey timeline. The narrative chapters carry no plant-wise capacity table, no project capex quantum, and no commissioning or ramp timeline for any named site; the only rupee capital figures in the routed text are the statutory named disclosures (segment capital expenditure and capital commitments) captured separately.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising adoption of intelligent electronics, advanced sensors, connected systems and software-led functionalities is significantly increasing the electronic content per vehicle.
- OEMs are increasingly adopting multi-powertrain strategies involving ICE, hybrid and EV platforms, so the pace of electrification transition remains uneven across markets and applications.
- FY26 growth was driven by increased business share across key OEM platforms, sustained leadership in ignition systems, growing momentum in Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) products, expansion of the electronic product portfolio and deeper penetration into premium vehicle segments.
- An improved sales mix with a higher contribution from exports and aftermarket (AFM) sales strengthened revenue quality and profitability; EBITDA was supported by material cost optimization initiatives and a favourable product mix.
- The aftermarket business remained an important growth driver, with both domestic and export aftermarket segments expanding market penetration and customer reach.
- Two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments recorded healthy growth, with premium motorcycles, scooters and electric mobility applications emerging as important growth drivers.
- GST reforms and rationalization measures boosted ICE platforms, while supply chain challenges and cost pressures moderated the pace of EV penetration in certain categories.
- GST 2.0, rolled out in September 2025 with simplified slabs of 5%, 18% and 40%, cut GST on small petrol/CNG cars (up to 1200cc) and motorcycles (up to 350cc) from 28% to 18% and moved hybrid vehicles into the 18% slab, accelerating adoption.
- The India-EU FTA concluded in January 2026 removes tariffs on 99.5% of traded goods including auto components, letting Indian Tier-1 suppliers export parts to European manufacturers without duty barriers.
- Indian retail vehicle sales reached a record ~2.97 crore units in 2025-26, a 13.3% year-on-year surge, propelled by GST 2.0 and the India-EU FTA.
- India's two-wheeler market was valued at USD 28.84 Billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 38.68 Billion by 2031 from USD 30.29 Billion in 2026, at a CAGR of 5.02%.
- ICE vehicles still dominate the Indian two-wheeler market at 88.15% of the market in 2025 on widespread fuel infrastructure and lower upfront costs, while electric two-wheelers are projected to grow at a 7.02% CAGR through 2026-2031.
- India's ICE market is projected to reach USD 8.3 Billion by 2031, expanding at a CAGR of 7.6% between 2025 and 2031, with demand steady despite the gradual shift to electrification.
- 'ICE 2.0' - modern ICE and hybrid powertrains are strengthening their relevance as key beneficiaries of recent tax reforms, offering a practical, cost-efficient solution for long-distance travel and rural mobility where EV charging infrastructure is still developing.
- India is emerging as a global export hub: passenger vehicle exports rose to nearly 9,00,000 units, up 16% year-on-year, and two-wheeler exports reached 5.1 Million units.
- Indian real GDP is projected to grow 7.6% in 2025-26, with 2026-27 growth expected to moderate to 6.6%-6.9% and a medium-term trajectory of around 7% through 2028; government infrastructure allocations rose to Rs 12.2 Lakh Crores from Rs 11.2 Lakh Crores.
- The 2026-27 global outlook points to moderate but fragile growth, with Middle East geopolitical tensions driving higher energy prices, elevated inflation and tighter financial conditions; IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.
- A sharp increase in commodity prices during the fourth quarter exerted pressure on margins; the Company also absorbed additional gratuity liability from the new labour code and market development expenses for future product lines including sensors.
- Freight cost escalations and continued depreciation of the Indian Rupee may exert pressure on margins in the near term; the Company remains focused on cost optimization, operational efficiency and strategic pricing actions.
- Rare-earth magnet shortages, volatility in electronic component availability, commodity price inflation and logistics disruptions remain operating constraints, and exports faced temporary disruptions from tariff burdens and global macroeconomic uncertainty, though management views the long-term export opportunity as highly promising.
- During 2025-26 the Company secured several important business wins across both domestic and export markets, further strengthening its growth pipeline and customer relationships; no order-book value is disclosed.
- Export programs for ignition systems and sensors gained traction in stationary engine applications, reflecting increasing customer confidence in INEL's engineering capabilities, product quality and cost competitiveness.

risks.note: MD&A Customer Risk: high dependence on a limited number of key customers can create vulnerabilities if these relationships change; in addition, limited awareness and proactive pursuit of emerging business opportunities could constrain growth prospects, and a relatively low export footprint elevates exposure to geopolitical risks, potentially affecting operations and profitability. BRSR names the major customers as TVS Motor Company Limited, Hero MotoCorp Limited and Bajaj Auto Limited, and puts the contribution of exports at 8% of total turnover. Mitigation is expanding market reach through direct sales and strategic partnerships alongside exploration of export opportunities, with dependency on key customers progressively reduced over the years.
risks.risk: Customer concentration and low export footprint

risks.note: MD&A Supplier Risk: heavy reliance on single-source vendors and limited geographic diversification among import suppliers creates supply chain risk; while lead times for electronic components have improved, automotive parts continue to face longer lead times. Mitigation is strategic sourcing initiatives for high-risk vendors and expanding indexation coverage for commodities not currently included in customer settlements.
risks.risk: Supplier concentration - single-source vendors and undiversified import base

risks.note: MD&A Input Cost Volatility Risk: fluctuating prices of silver and electronic components can increase production costs and pressure profit margins; mitigation is long-term supplier agreements, VAVE, strategic inventory management and continuous cost monitoring. The Board's Report adds that a sharp increase in commodity prices during the fourth quarter exerted pressure on margins, that freight cost escalations and continued depreciation of the Indian Rupee may exert pressure on margins in the near term, and that the Company is pursuing compensation from customers through price revisions and indexing arrangements for currently non-indexed commodities.
risks.risk: Input cost volatility - silver and electronic components

risks.note: MD&A Technology Risk: rapid technological change necessitates continuous innovation and adaptability; heightened EV competition from both established players as well as startups underscores the importance of differentiation; and there is a significant risk of product obsolescence as evolving technologies require ongoing upgrades to sustain market relevance. The industry section adds that electrification, connected mobility and software-defined vehicles demand significant and sustained capital investment, and that players lacking scale, localization capabilities or financial resilience may struggle to remain competitive. Mitigation: strategic technology partnerships in specialized areas, leveraging OEM relationships, and ongoing R&D investment.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and the EV transition

risks.note: MD&A Geopolitical Risk: tensions between the US and China have heightened rare earth supply chain risks, and maritime disruptions in the Red Sea driven by West Asia conflicts have intensified logistical delays and increased input costs, creating a highly challenging operating environment; the mitigation note also cites anticipated impacts arising from labor code reforms. Mitigation is execution excellence, disciplined cost optimization including Value Analysis and Value Engineering (VAVE), and increased adoption of ferrite magnets as an alternative to rare earth materials. The Board's Report confirms West Asia developments contributed to inflationary pressures and supply chain constraints in the availability of certain raw materials, and BRSR lists Global Geo-political as a material risk-and-opportunity issue with a plan in place to de-risk the supply chain.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption - rare earth supply chain and Red Sea logistics

risks.note: MD&A industry section: increasing reliance on semiconductors and battery-grade critical minerals, concentrated within limited global geographies, exposes the industry to supply-side vulnerabilities; while Indian OEMs demonstrated relative resilience during the pandemic, the shift toward electrified and software-driven architectures materially amplifies this risk.
risks.risk: Semiconductor and critical mineral dependency concentrated in limited geographies

risks.note: MD&A IT and Cyber Risk states existing measures to protect confidential and sensitive information from internal and external threats are currently inadequate, and BRSR lists Data Security and Privacy as a material risk citing an inadequate information security and cyber framework. Mitigation: a completed Security Incident and Event Management audit with corrective measures implemented, a successfully completed Information Security Management System surveillance audit, regular cybersecurity awareness programmes, and audit trails established across all critical business applications. No security breaches or system outages were reported during the year.
risks.risk: IT and cyber risk - protective measures stated to be currently inadequate

risks.note: MD&A People Risk: challenges in attracting and retaining top talent may impact long-term growth, and a misalignment between the organizational structure and strategic objectives could affect operational efficiency. BRSR discloses a permanent employee turnover rate of 15.68% in 2025-26 versus 15.19% in 2024-25 (permanent workers nil). Mitigation is strengthening employer branding, enhancing training and development programs to build leadership capabilities, and a focused approach on defining key result areas.
risks.risk: People risk - talent attraction, retention and organisational alignment
